 Judgment
These appeal and Cross-objection are filed challenging the judgment dated 08.02.2016 passed in
M.V.C.No.180/2014 on the file of the Itinerary Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims
Tribunal at H
osadurga ('the Tribunal' in short).
2. M.F.A.No.3262/2016 is filed by the Insurance Company whereas Cross-objection No.94/2016 is filed by the petitioners.
Appellant was the second respondent, respondent Nos.1 and 2 are petitioners and respondent No.3 was respondent No.1 before the Tribunal.
The parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

M/S New India Assurance Company vs Smt Thimmamma on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49473907/
3 3.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company vs Smt Thimmamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Briefly stated the facts are that, on 03.05.2010 at about 5.00 p.m., one Mahalingappa (in short 'the deceased'), the husband of petitioner No.1 and father of petitioner No.2, while riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-03/EF-9602 as a pillion rider, near a nursery at Chowdipalya, due to rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle, he fell down from the motor cycle, sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to death on the way to NIMHANS Hospital, Bangalore near Tiptur.
The petitioners have approached the Tribunal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.27,80,000/- with interest at 18% per annum.
Claim was opposed by the respondents.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.9,04,000/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum, directing the Insurance Company to pay the compensation.
Aggrieved by the award, the Insurance Company has filed this appeal and the petitioners being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation have filed cross-objections on various grounds.

4. I have heard the arguments of Sri.A.M.Venkatesh, learned counsel for the appellant/insurer and Sri.N.D.Manjunath, learned counsel for the petitioners.
5.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that petitioner No.2 is the major son of deceased, who is not a dependent.
The deceased was though aged 65 years, it was not properly considered, for the age of 65, applicable multiplier is '7' as against '11' applied by the Tribunal.
The deceased was not an earning member of the family, the Tribunal erred in deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses as there is no proof of income for the deceased.

Petitioner No.1 is a BPL card holder in the year 2012 showing that the family income is less than Rs.12,000/- per annum and therefore, Rs.8,000/- per month taken by the Tribunal without any basis and the compensation is awarded in excess of the entitlement and sought for interference by this court.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that the petitioners have placed evidence explaining that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/- per month and inspite of it, the Tribunal has assessed lesser compensation, which needs modification and the compensation awarded towards conventional heads needs to be enhanced.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of accident and death occurred on account of the accidental injuries.

On perusal of the impugned judgment, it is pertinent to note that the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month for the purpose of calculating the loss of dependency and awarded a sum of Rs.7,04,000/- towards loss of dependency, Rs.1,00,000/-
towards loss of consortium, Rs.75,000/- towards loss of love and affection and Rs.25,000/- towards transportation charges.

The reasons assigned by the Tribunal is not correct insofar as the assessment of compensation under conventional heads, as the law has already been settled that towards conventional heads, the compensation should not be exaggerated.
The claim made by the petitioners shall not be a windfall at the cost of tax payers money and at the same time, it shall be just compensation the victims are entitled to.

4 9.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company vs Smt Thimmamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Adverting to the arguments of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company with reference to the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in New India Assurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Vinish Jain and Others1, it is pertinent to note that in the present case, wife is a dependant and major son has also joined the mother in claiming compensation, who is entitled only under conventional heads i.e.,
towards (2018) 3 SCC 619 loss of love and affection.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Vinish Jain and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Vinish Jain's case (supra), the claim was made by two major sons, there were no dependants.

Under such circumstances, deduction of 50%
was allowed by the Hon'ble Apex Court and it cannot be applied to this case.

Hence, the principles laid down in Vinish Jain's case will not come to the aid of the Insurance Company in asking 50%
deduction towards personal expenses.
10. Another point canvassed by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company is that, the deceased was aged 65 years and income of the deceased taken at Rs.8,000/- is not correct.

In this regard, the Insurance Company has relied upon the BPL card obtained by petitioner No.1 in the year 2012, but the accident was in the year 2010 and therefore, it is quite natural that the family fall under BPL for losing an earning member of the family and therefore, ration card was issued.
It cannot be a guiding document for assessment of the income of the deceased.

11. As regarding the age is concerned, the postmortem report clearly points out that the deceased was aged 55 years and in the year 2010, the age of the first petitioner is shown as 50 years, in these circumstances, in the absence of controverting material, I do not find any discrepancy.

Therefore,
the age of '55' years assessed by the Tribunal is proper.
12. Admittedly, the accident was of the year 2010.
The petitioners though claimed that the deceased was an agriculturist and doing business, there is no proof of income placed before the Tribunal.
In the year 2010, the probable income of a person who has no proof of income is generally assessed at Rs.5,5,00/-.
Applying the principles of National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others2 case, the future prospects of 10% has to be added to the income of the deceased as he was aged more than 55 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The deceased left behind dependent wife, hence, 1/3rd deduction is effected towards personal expenses, the loss of dependency would come to Rs.5,32,488/- (Rs.5,500/-+Rs.550/-
=Rs.6,050/- - 1/3rd = Rs.2016 = Rs.4,034x12x11).
13.

Towards loss of love and affection, a sum of Rs.20,000/- each is assessed, a sum of Rs.10,000/-
towards loss of estate and Rs.10,000/- towards funeral expenses.

Thus, the just compensation that the petitioners are entitled to, in the facts and circumstances of the case will Rs.6,32,488/- as against Rs.9,09,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, thereby the quantum of compensation has to be reduced by Rs.2,76,512/-, it is just and (2017) 16 SCC 680 adequate compensation in the facts and circumstances of the case.
The Cross-Objection filed by the petitioners is devoid of merits and is liable to be dismissed and the appeal filed by the Insurance Company deserves to be allowed.

In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) M.F.A.No.3262/2016 filed by the Insurance Company is allowed in part.

sentences.text: (iii) The impugned judgment stands modified.

(iii) The petitioners/cross-objectors would be entitled to compensation of Rs.6,32,488/- as against Rs.9,09,000/- awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
(iv) The Insurance Company is directed to satisfy the award within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
